newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine c. bank wants convertible currency in '97.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine c. bank wants convertible currency in '97.

text.p: Ukraine is set to make the hryvnia a convertible currency but must first wait until parliament passes the 1997 budget, the central bank chairman said late on Tuesday.
"We cannot have a convertible currency without a solid budget," Viktor Yushchenko said at a news conference.

The central bank has proposed allowing non-resident banks to freely buy hard currency on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange (UICE) and the interbank market starting in 1997, but the budget must be passed before this can happen.
Non-resident banks are allowed to sell hard currency and can convert hryvnia earned from the sale of Treasury bills.
The draft budget is being reviewed by parliament and will probably be passed between January and March, though the new constitution states it must be accepted by January 1.
Yushchenko said the move would bring Ukraine closer to adhering to Article 8 of the International Monetary Fund charter, which would formally designate the currency as convertible.
He said no decision was yet made on a currency regime for the hryvnia, whose rate is currently set on the UICE.

The central bank said previously that it was considering one of two regimes for the hryvnia, either pegging it in a narrow range against a single hard currency or linking it more loosely to a currency or basket of currencies.
The hryvnia, introduced on September 2, replaced the interim karbovanets currency.
